items.title: Eddie Metz Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, October 3, 2015
items.q: we played bossa novas, we played rumbas, we played cha-chas, we played straight ahead jazz songs, Duke Ellington ballads.

ctx.x: Yeah so that was what kind of jazz?

Well it was what we call club dates. Standards for dancing at a country club in Ann Arbor, Michigan. So we played bossa novas, we played rumbas, we played cha-chas, we played straight ahead jazz songs, Duke Ellington ballads. Nothing too fast, nothing too slow. It was businessman’s bounce. You know, and ballads were like [scats and snaps fingers]. That was about as slow as it got. And then the faster tune [scats and snaps fingers]. It was for dancing. Nothing too fast. Nothing too slow. So that’s where I really…
the Beatles and, you know, whoever else was popular in the 60s and 70s and I love that music also. In fact I just did a rock & roll record last year.
